710466.t: Uncertain. Commonly connected with Latin foedus (“ugly”).

710443.t: Unknown; in the absence of an explanation, Beekes prefers a Pre-Greek borrowing, noting that Meier-Brügger's derivation from a Proto-Indo-European *per-trom (“instrument for getting through”) (from *per- (“to go through, fare”) + *-trom (“instrument…

710478.t: From Proto-Indo-European *peh₃- (“to drink”). Cognates include Sanskrit पिब॑ति (píbati), Latin pōtō and bibō, and Albanian pi.

710484.t: From Proto-Indo-European *bʰéydʰtis, equivalent to πείθω (peíthō, “to persuade”) + -τις (-tis). Compare the later formation, πεῖσις (peîsĭs).

710481.t: From Proto-Hellenic *píptō, from Proto-Indo-European *pípth₂-, reduplicated present from *peth₂- (“to fall; to fly”). For an unknown reason, the iota is long, as is apparent from the imperative πῖπτε (not **πίπτε (**pĭ́pte)).

710439.t: From πέτομαι (pétomai, “to fly”) from Proto-Indo-European *péth₂eti from the root *peth₂- (literally “to spread one’s wings”).

710408.t: From περιφερής (peripherḗs, “circular; rounded; revolving; wavering”) + -ια (-ia), from περιφέρω (periphérō, “to carry round; revolve; wander”), from περι- (peri-, “around, surrounding”) + φέρω (phérō, “to carry, bear”) from Proto-Hellenic *pʰérō (“to…

710486.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pitstós, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰidʰtós. By surface analysis, πιθ- (pith-) (zero-grade of the root of πείθω (peíthō, “to persuade; to trust”)) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

710498.t: πλανάω (planáō, “to wander”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent noun suffix)

710433.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

710495.t: Uncertain. Mechanically reconstructable as a thematization of a nasal present *pl-néh₂-ti, corresponding to Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂- (“flat, broad”), but the semantics are highly problematic.

710475.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pikrós, formally identical to Proto-Slavic *pьstrъ (“variegated”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *piḱ-rós, from the root *peyḱ- (“color, speckle”).

710493.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *pleth₂-? Proto-Indo-European *pel-? Proto-Indo-European *pleh₂-der. Ancient Greek πλάγος (plágos) Proto-Indo-European *-yósder.

710452.t: From Proto-Indo-European *peh₂ǵ- (“to coagulate, become fixed”). Cognates include Latin pangō and Old English fōn (English fang).

710441.t: From Proto-Indo-European *péth₂eti (“to fly”), from the root *peth₂- (literally “to spread one’s wings”).

710435.t: From Proto-Indo-European *peth₂- (“to spread out”). Cognates include Albanian petë, Old English fæþm (English fathom), Latin pateō, patulus and pandō; and Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬚𐬀𐬥𐬀 (paθana).

710446.t: Of Pre-Greek origin. Related to πέτρα (pétra, “rock formation”).

710457.t: Of unknown origin, with Beekes tentatively suspecting a derivation from Pre-Greek, albeit with no particular evidence.

710482.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pít͏̌t͏̌a, from Proto-Indo-European *pik- (“pitch, resin”). Cognate with Latin pix, Proto-Slavic *pьkъlъ.

710462.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pā́kʰus, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeh₂ǵʰús. Cognates include Sanskrit बाहु (bāhu, “arm”), Old Persian 𐎲𐎠𐏀𐎢 (b-a-z-u /⁠bāzu⁠/) (Persian بازو (bâzu)), and Old English bōg (English bough).

710460.t: Unclear, though probably from Pre-Greek; possible connection with Latin pero (“soldier's shoes”).

710496.t: Back-formation from πλανάω (planáō, “to wander, to roam”).

710454.t: Deverbative or denominative formation on the basis of a form *pēd-, which appears to be a lengthened grade of Proto-Indo-European *ped- (“to walk, step”).

710455.t: From Proto-Indo-European *kʷo- (“interrogative, relative stem”) and maybe *h₂el- (“to grow”). Cognate with Latin quālis.

710465.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *peysd- (“to squeeze”), and cognate with Sanskrit पीडयति (pīḍáyati). The Indo-European root may be a d-extension of *peys- (“to grind, crush”), though such an enlargement is strange.

710467.t: Like many Greek words for pottery, most likely of Pre-Greek origin, as evidenced by the irregular variations between: * δ ~ θ (d ~ th), the former as in e.g. πίδος (pídos) * π ~ φ (p ~ ph), as in the derived terms πιθάκνη (pitháknē) ~ φιδάκνη (phidáknē)…

710480.t: Syncopic form of *πιπεράσκω (*pĭperā́skō); from *πιπεράω (*pĭperắō, reduplication of περάω (perắō, “to export for sale”)) + -σκω (-skō).

710491.t: From Proto-Indo-European *peyH- (“fat”). Cognate with Latin pīnguis (“fat; plump”) and Proto-Germanic *faitaz (“fat”).

710489.t: The formation is like λέπυρον (lépuron), but without a certain explanation. It has been connected to Latin putus (“pure”), Sanskrit पूत (pūtá, “cleansed”) and Proto-Germanic *faujaną (“to sift”), but this is highly unlikely.

710490.t: Beekes is hesitant to espouse any derivation (even the usual Pre-Greek) and leaves the origin open.

710459.t: From πήγνυμι (pḗgnumi, “I stick, I fix”) + -σις (-sis, suffix to form a feminine noun).

710400.t: From περι- (peri-, “around”) + τειχίζω (teikhízō, “to build a wall”)

710463.t: A conflation of πιέζω (piézō, “squeeze”) and βιάζομαι (biázomai, “force”).
